claimed_value: GPT-4 agents (project manager plus tech agents) turn commands into structured JSON configurations that drive role functions: inpainting for deletion, asset bank, motion generation, view adjustment

Command execution success rates over 5 instruction categories (15 commands, 3 trials each); motion-from-text user study: ChatSim 0.988 straight, 0.940 left turn, 0.976 right turn, 0.952 speed, 1.000 within-road, versus GPT2Code and GPT2Motion.
Historical Gaussians are aligned by ego motion, new areas completed with random Gaussians, then refined by an evolution layer with sparse convolution and deformable attention to image features
not applicable, no control input. Prediction gain: mIoU +2.4% and IoU +2.7% over single-frame GaussianFormer-B; ablations on ego motion and dynamic-object factors
Canonical ray-maps and reference frames given as conditions C to a panoramic diffusion transformer; denoising on a joint latent of channel-concatenated RGB, semantics and depth
Camera-control error on 150 nuScenes validation scenes: 1.18 m TransErr versus 7.56 m for UniScene; zero-shot nuPlan TransErr 1.65 versus 7.12 for DiST-4D
Adaptive layer norm for actions and timesteps, additive embeddings for camera parameters, decoupled cross-attention branches for dynamic agents, static elements and text
Qualitative action-controllability figure: logged versus generated video with ego trajectory for next 3 s overlaid (for example Turn Right to Turn Left); no number in packet
Lightweight control branch: small MLP encodes simulator state into control tokens concatenated with visual tokens (no ControlNet); text by cross-attention; streaming KV cache gives memory.
Fidelity as a simulator: policy ranking by All Incidents under NuRec is preserved under OmniDreams, with OmniDreams WAM best and Alpamayo 1.5 (1 cam) worst, called a faithful proxy.
token conditioning: image and action tokens form one unified vocabulary and sequence, modelled by next-token prediction with causal attention and frame-wise 1D rotary embeddings

Table 1 on navtest: FVD 142.61 and FID 12.78 versus fine-tuned SVD 227.54 and 24.03. Action-condition understanding in long videos shown qualitatively; PDMS 65.3 to 82.4 with position embedding on actions.

ego-motion embeddings are added to learned world queries (one group per future frame, with frame embedding) processed by the LLM, then cross-attention link to future BEV features and a point-cloud renderer
No dedicated action-following test in packet. Generation accuracy: Chamfer 3s 1.17 versus 1.73 for ViDAR (about 32% lower), and 1.37 for a separated unification variant.
BEV layout is tokenised by a VQ-VAE; an autoregressive transformer attends globally to BEV tokens, with camera-derived spatial embeddings and a pairwise camera attention bias
CVT on generated images: road mIoU 50.20, vehicle mIoU 5.89 (real-image model: 66.31 and 27.51); FID 25.54 on nuScenes; augmentation adds 0.6 mIoU road and vehicle

Bi-Directional Modulated Transformer: condition-to-latent and latent-to-condition cross-attention with temporal self-attention, injected into the UNet; condition features come from convolutional encoders.

Perception on generated validation data drops only slightly from real: Road mIoU 64.43 (-9.25), Vehicle mIoU 28.86 (-5.98), Object NDS 36.5 (-4.71). FID 8.34, FVD 76.39. Qualitative map and layout edits shown.

Lightweight trajectory encoder (two attention blocks, linear head) feeds waypoints into the DiT input alongside video latents; command via T5 text; command dropped with p=0.5 for classifier-free guidance.
Waymo zero-shot Trajectory Difference (Table 1): action-free 1.13 vs Vista 5.68; expert action 0.86 vs 1.89 (GT future 0.58). Human study favors ReSim on non-expert action following.

BEV layout concatenated with noise volumes in an occupancy DiT; occupancy rendered to depth and semantic maps and injected into video U-Net via ControlNet-style branch; text by cross-attention; layout editing via DDIM inversion

Layout edits shown qualitatively; mIoU is used to check layout accuracy of generated outputs. Reported gains versus prior SOTA: Figure 1 shows 41.4% lower video FVD, 71.1% lower occupancy error and 31.6% lower LiDAR MMD.

two stages: risk embedded by MLP and applied by FiLM to BEV features of a GenAD-style motion generator; resulting trajectories and boxes injected as structured motion conditions into the diffusion backbone
Paper says measured risk closely matches target but omits the analysis; qualitative quantiles 0.95, 0.8, 0.2. Fidelity: FID 15.70 versus 20.91, mAP 30.50 versus 18.17.
